reasoning: B builds the shadows, glow and inner shadow natively with UIShadow, tiles the hex pattern, uses flex layout and sprite sheets, and its asset plan meets the size limits. A bakes the shadows and glow into images, stretches an oversized hex image and has no sprite sheet. Both work with live data, but B matches the design and the native-versus-image plan much more closely.

criteria.note: The panel shadow and the slot glow are 9-slice images (Image.PanelShadow, Image.SlotGlow), and the doc lists them as images; the text shadows are offset label copies, not UIShadow.
The HexPattern ImageLabel uses ScaleType.Stretch with a 1440x760 image baked to the panel's shape, not a tile, though it does sit outside the list layout.
Vertical UIListLayout with Padding 16, UIPadding 24/28, UIGridLayout with CellSize 96 and CellPadding 12; the header uses anchor points instead of flex but looks the same; the name is sized 1,-216.
BackgroundTransparency 0.08, gradients at Rotation 90 on a white base, Inner/Outer strokes at 2/1/3 px, correct radii.
No UIShadow anywhere; the inner shadow is faked with a 3 px shorter face, the shadows are images, and the fill isn't darkened to make up for the missing blur.
One InventorySlot component driven by IsLocked/IsSelected from BlockInventory; locked art at ImageTransparency 0.6; the grid keeps slots in place.
The hex export is over 1024 px, the shadows are 1x, there is no sprite sheet for the block art, and the icons are white and tinted; ids are in one module.
All checks pass, Equip calls BlockPlacer.setBlockType, and the panel follows BlockTypeChanged and BlockInventory.Changed.
UIShadow for the panel, glow, inset shadow and text shadows; the doc lists only the block art sheet, the icon sheet and the hex tile.
ScaleType.Tile with TileSize 112x192 in offsets, absolutely positioned inside the panel and outside the Content list layout.
HorizontalFlex SpaceBetween header, UIGridLayout 96/12, UIFlexItem Fill on the footer name next to the 200x52 button.
Gradients at Rotation 90 on a white base, BorderStrokePosition Inner/Outer with 2/1/3 px, radii 16/12/full.
Panel UIShadow (0,12, blur 32, 0.55), Inset UIShadow on Equip, Mode=Text shadows, glow UIShadow, Surface transparency 0.04 standing in for the blur.
One slot component with IsSelected/IsLocked props fed from BlockInventory through readSlots; contentTransparency 0.6 when locked.
2x exports all under 1024 px, an 880x352 block sprite sheet using ImageRectOffset, white icons tinted with ImageColor3, all ids in InventoryAssets.
Checks pass and Equip calls setBlockType, but it rewrote the Screen.luau fixture and added extras such as fit scaling and an open button.

strengths: Clean, working Vide code with live data
weaknesses: Image shadows and glow instead of UIShadow
Stretched, oversized hex image instead of a tile
No sprite sheet; export sizes break the limits

strengths: Uses native UIShadow, tiling and flex exactly as the rubric asks
Sprite sheets and a well-planned asset module
Panel kept separate from game data, with stories
weaknesses: Scope creep (fit scale, open button, extra Equip states)
